Let the tangent line $l$ have intercepts $N(a,0)$ and $M(0,b)$, so its equation is $\frac{x}{a}+\frac{y}{b}=1$. Since $l$ is tangent to $x^2+y^2=1$, the distance from the origin to $l$ equals $1$:
$$\frac{1}{\sqrt{\frac1{a^2}+\frac1{b^2}}}=1 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \frac1{a^2}+\frac1{b^2}=1.$$

Set $u=\frac1a$, $v=\frac1b$, so $u^2+v^2=1$. With $A(3,4)$ and $C(0,0)$,
$$\overrightarrow{AC}=(-3,-4),\quad \overrightarrow{AM}=(-3,b-4),\quad \overrightarrow{AN}=(a-3,-4).$$

From $\overrightarrow{AC}=x\overrightarrow{AM}+y\overrightarrow{AN}$ we obtain the system
$$\begin{cases}-3=-3x+y(a-4)\\-4=x(b-4)-4y\end{cases}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad \begin{cases}ay=3(x+y)-3\\ bx=4(x+y)-4.\end{cases}$$

Let $t=x+y$. Then $x=\dfrac{4(t-1)}{b}$, $y=\dfrac{3(t-1)}{a}$, and substituting back gives
$$t=(t-1)\left(\frac3a+\frac4b\right)=(t-1)K,\qquad K:=3u+4v.$$
Hence $t=\dfrac{K}{K-1}$, so $t-1=\dfrac1{K-1}$ and therefore
$$x=\frac{4v}{K-1},\qquad y=\frac{3u}{K-1}.$$

Now compute
$$9x^2+16y^2=\frac{144v^2+144u^2}{(K-1)^2}=\frac{144(u^2+v^2)}{(K-1)^2}=\frac{144}{(K-1)^2}.$$

Since $u^2+v^2=1$, by Cauchy–Schwarz $K=3u+4v\in[-5,5]$. Thus $(K-1)^2\le (-5-1)^2=36$, with equality when $(u,v)=\left(-\frac35,-\frac45\right)$. Consequently
$$9x^2+16y^2\ge\frac{144}{36}=4.$$

The minimum is attained for the tangent line $3x+4y=-5$, which indeed meets both axes.

$$\boxed{4}$$
